title: storage-provisioner-module-v2: unified EBS/EFS/S3 provisioning with encrypted defaults
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Build v2 of the storage provisioner Terraform module tailored for Private (VPC) deployments. Goals: provide a single modular interface to provision EBS volumes, EFS filesystems, and S3 buckets with secure-by-default configurations (encryption at rest, enforced KMS usage, block public access for S3), snapshot lifecycle policies, and health-check hooks for the Private control plane. The module should enable safe in-place upgrades from the existing v1 stack, expose sane inputs for performance/cost tuning, and emit outputs needed by node bootstrap and backup operators.

Scope:
- Resources: EBS (gp3, encrypted by default), EFS (throughput/mode defaults, encrypted, access point optional), S3 (bucket hardening, default bucket policy to deny non-TLS and block public access), snapshot lifecycle automation for EBS and EFS backups, optional cross-region replication for S3.
- Defaults: default to customer-managed KMS keys when provided, otherwise create CMKs with key policy scoped to account and InfraOps role. Require explicit enablement for public bucket flags.
- Health checks: add lightweight Lambda-based probes and output SSM/console-ready status entries used by the Private control plane to verify mountability, encryption integrity, and snapshot readiness.
- Upgrade path: migration plan to move existing unencrypted resources to encrypted ones using snapshot/restore workflow, with automation scripts and phasing to avoid downtime.
- Tests & validation: unit tests using kitchen-terraform/terratest, a staged apply runbook, and a canary deploy in a dedicated staging VPC.

Why this work: several customers deploying Private VPC clusters have asked for a hardened, opinionated storage IaC module that reduces onboarding time and eliminates common misconfigurations that caused incidents last year (see postmortem ENG-29870). This module centralizes defaults, reduces drift, and plugs into Redwood Private observability/health backlog for faster troubleshooting.
comments: 2025-02-13 - Avery Chen: Kickoff meeting notes attached to Confluence link. Agreed module should prefer CMK supplied by customer; auto-CMK only if missing. Decided to support EBS gp3 defaults and EFS general purpose throughput mode.

2025-02-18 - Marcus Patel: Prototype branch created. Initial HCL skeleton covers ebs/efs/s3 and includes kms_key_id optional input. Ran a dry-plan against staging - observed that default S3 block_public_access resource is incompatible with an existing cross-account replication role; added opt-out flag. Opened PR #678 for early feedback.

2025-02-21 - Sofia Ruiz (Security): Reviewed IAM/KMS policy draft. Requested explicit key usage restrictions and audit key rotation docs. Marked security_review_required=true. Also called out that module must not create overly permissive roles; suggested calling out a minimal InfraOps role in README.

2025-02-24 - Marcus Patel: Implemented snapshot lifecycle for EBS (Data Lifecycle Manager) and EFS (backup plan via AWS Backup). Added optional retention_window_days input and default 30 days. Noted trade-off: AWS Backup adds cost; left opt-in with default true for Private customers.

acceptance_criteria: Module provisions EBS/EFS/S3 with encryption-by-default in a staging VPC without manual overrides
Upgrade path validated: existing unencrypted EBS volume can be migrated using snapshot-and-restore automation with <5m perceived downtime for attached instances (tested in staging)
Health checks report mountability and snapshot readiness to Private control plane endpoints
All IAM and KMS policies pass security review and least-privilege checks
Automated tests run in CI and a manual canary apply executed in staging with sign-off
implementation_notes: Implementation will be split into a root module (storage-provisioner) that calls submodules: ebs, efs, s3, kms. Keep submodules small and publish to infra-modules registry for reuse.
Default KMS behaviour: if kms_key_id is null, create CMK with description 'redwood:private:storage:v2' and key admins set to InfraOps role and root. Expose key_arn as output.

S3 defaults: enforce server-side encryption AES256 or aws:kms depending on kms_key_id. Always enable block_public_acls, block_public_policy and restrict public access by default. Provide override 'allow_public_bucket' for migration cases.

Upgrade plan: for EBS, create snapshot of existing volume, create encrypted volume from snapshot, attach, and update attachment gracefully. Provide automation script using AWS SDK with safety checks. For S3, use aws s3 cp + replication if needed but encourage bucket-by-bucket migration and update bucket policies.

Health checks: small Lambda in Terraform using a lightweight Go runtime to attempt mount (for EFS) or HEAD request (for S3) and emit status to CloudWatch and a Private control plane SNS topic. Allow customers to opt out.
Testing: use a dedicated staging account and VPC. Include smoke tests that validate encryption flag, kms key presence, and snapshot retention behavior. Record diffs for review.
Compatibility: maintain backwards compatibility for inputs used by existing stacks; if incompatible changes are required, provide shims and a migration guide with example commands.
